environment.description: Same Flask application deployed in a hardened container on RHEL 9 with a custom SELinux type enforcement policy (myapp_flask_t). The policy module was compiled with checkmodule and loaded via semodule. The type myapp_flask_t is assigned to the process context via container_runtime_t transition. The TE policy contains: allow myapp_flask_t myapp_data_t:file { read write create unlink }; allow myapp_flask_t myapp_data_t:dir { read write add_name remove_name search }; with file context spec /var/lib/myapp/userdata(/.*)? mapping to myapp_data_t and /var/lib/myapp/exports(/.*)? mapping to myapp_export_t. Critically, the write permission for myapp_export_t is constrained: allow myapp_flask_t myapp_export_t:file { write create } only when the path matches the labeled context. Any write attempt to paths outside /var/lib/myapp/userdata/ and /var/lib/myapp/exports/ results in AVC denial. The container also runs with --security-opt=no-new-privileges and drops CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE. Additionally, the Podman container uses a seccomp profile that permits only the specific syscalls needed (no chmod, chown, or symlink creation).

config.selinux_policy: custom myapp_flask_t type enforcement module v1.2
config.te_rules: allow myapp_flask_t myapp_data_t:file { read write create unlink open getattr }; allow myapp_flask_t myapp_export_t:file { write create open getattr }; allow myapp_flask_t myapp_export_t:dir { write add_name search };
config.note: CSRF vulnerability still present in application code; SELinux MAC policy limits blast radius of export_path manipulation
